_comment: Which rail each capacitor sits on, and what that rail runs at.
The rated voltage is NOT here -- it is read from the parts list
at run time, so a corrected BOM corrects this too.
source: 'schematic' means the net was traced on the Chapter 7
sheet cited in the note; 'inferred' means it was deduced from
the rails present at that slot and has not been read off a
schematic. appliedV: null means the rail was never traced --
shown as unknown rather than assumed safe.
railClass is how much energy is behind the rail, which decides
what a shorted part does: A is an unfused 3 A rail with a
6600 uF reservoir, C is fused, E is a floating common.

C55.net: U60 (7705A) CT timing pin to GND2
C55.note: CORRECTED 2026-08 by the tantalum audit; was '+5V dig, 5.2 V, inferred, | A19, fused F5 3.15A'. Both halves of that were wrong. Traced on Figure 7-21 sheet 2 of 2 (Ch7 PDF page 81), in the POWER UP AND RESET CIRCUITRY block: C55 is not a decoupler at all, it is the CT timing capacitor of U60, a 7705A supervisor. Its top plate is the CT node -- U60 pin 3, with R52 (1 kOhm 1 %) and the RESET SWITCH SW51 on it -- and its bottom plate is GND2. The sheet annotates the block TIME CONSTANT IS 130 mSEC. In service the CT node ramps well below the rail, so 5.1 V is recorded as the hard upper bound the +5V rail sets, not as an operating value. 51 % of a 10 V part at that bound and less in practice. What matters for this one is capacitance rather than voltage: a dried-out C55 shortens or loses the power-on reset pulse.

C58.note: CORRECTED 2026-08; was 5.2 V 'inferred', sourced to A19. Traced on Figure 7-21 sheet 2 of 2 (Ch7 PDF page 81): C58 (10 uF) is the bulk member of the row captioned BYPASS CAPACITORS -- C102, C104, C105, C106, C107, C109, C110, C112, C113 at 0.1 uF each, then C58 -- strung across the guarded section's +5V rail to GND2, feeding the 637A01Y0 microcontroller and the 74HC glue around it. The rail is NOT A19's +5 V; see C57, which traces its origin on this same sheet. +5 LH is +5.1 V +/-300 mV (Table 2-10, TP11), so 5.1 V nominal and 5.4 V worst case, i.e. 51 % and 54 % of a 10 V part. Marginal either way.

C57.net: +5V (guarded digital), derived on this board from +5 LH through L51
C57.note: CORRECTED 2026-08, and this entry carries the evidence for C55 and C58 as well. Was '+5V dig, 5.2 V, inferred, | A19, fused F5 3.15A'. Figure 7-21 sheet 2 of 2 (Ch7 PDF page 81), bottom left, in the block captioned INPUT POWER FILTER, draws the whole thing: '+5LH FROM SHEET 1' arrives, passes through L51 (3 turns), and the node beyond it is labelled +5V and brought out to TP52 VCC2, with C54 (0.1 uF), C57 (47 uF) and C59 (0.1 uF) returning to LH COM / TP55 GND2. So the guarded digital section's +5 V is made on A17 from A17's own +5 LH output; it does not come from A19's digital supply and F5 is not its fuse. The magnitude barely moves -- A19's +5 V is 5.2 V +/-5 % (Table 2-2) and A17's +5 LH is 5.1 V +/-300 mV (Table 2-10) -- but the fault path does: the regulator behind this rail is U8 on THIS assembly, a 2 A TO-3 with no fuse in front of it, so a shorted C57 is A17's own problem and will not blow anything on A19. 51 % of a 10 V part at nominal, 54 % at the top of the band. It is also the largest capacitor in the guarded section, so the one whose capacitance loss shows up first.
